comments.text: Honestly, the small improvements from Amtrak (the 1% improvements) have made a huge difference. Even things like newer trainsets and more frequent service matter. I relied on Amtrak for about a year, and probably 1 in 5 trains were delayed, sometimes badly. Even on NJ Transit into New York, you’ve gotta expect a delay.

comments.author: @eottoe2001
comments.text: The thing that would make these state support routes work better would be if they could average 100 mph overall. While not a super high speed, it is a speed that is doable with current equipment, tech, and welded rail. We need to consider that not all European or Asian rail is rolling at 189 mph, but a lot is just doing something like 50 to 60 mph, believe it or not, for intercity rail. 100 mph would be a game-changing system-wide for Amtrak and VIA Rail. It would be something to consider: limiting freight train length on Amtrak-used rail lines so passing sidings could be utilized. I know this doesn't fit the movement-conservative idea of no regulation for anything, but as we are witnessing, those ideas from Reagan and Milton Friedman don't work. Reality and adultness do. Great video.
